Title: The Last Letter

Characters

Raghuveer (78 years) (very thin old man, back bent, deep wrinkles, thick white moustache, old khaki kurta-pyjama with small holes, bare cracked feet, thick black square glasses)

Pari (7 years) (round chubby face, big black eyes, two small plaits with red ribbons, blue school uniform shirt and skirt with mud stains)

Objects

Grandfather's wooden stick (4 feet long, dark brown old wood, the handle black and smooth)

Pari's pink school bag (small faded pink bag, torn, the zip open)

Yellowed old letter (6x4 inch yellowed paper, folded once, written in blue ink: for Bapu)

Broken wooden bench (4 feet long old dark brown bench, one front leg broken, a brick under it)

Old red post box (3 feet tall iron box, rusted, a long slit in front)

Dust and dry leaves on the ground (brown earth with hundreds of dry neem leaves)

Places and Backgrounds

Old village post office - outside (one-storey old yellow building, peeling plaster, closed wooden doors, harsh sun at 2 pm)

Corner under the neem tree (ten steps in front of the post office, deep cool shade, the broken bench is here)

Sky and wind (clear blue sky, warm light wind, birds far away)

Story

Scene 1
(2 pm, the corner under the neem tree in front of the old post office, sunlight falls through the leaves in round spots, Raghuveer sits on the broken bench, he holds the wooden stick with both hands, his glasses have slipped down his nose, the rusted red post box is in front of him)

Raghuveer: "It did not come today either... fifteen years now." (softly, in a very tired trembling voice, looking at the post box without blinking, then he lowers his head slowly)

Scene 2
(Same place, the dirt road behind, Pari comes running down the road, her pink school bag bounces on her back, she stops right at the red post box and reaches out to touch it, Raghuveer is startled, his head jerks up)

Raghuveer: "Hey, who is that? Don't touch the post box." (a little annoyed, his voice shaking)

Pari: "I am Pari! Why do you sit on this broken bench every day, Grandpa?" (with a big smile, playful voice)

(Pari puts her bag on the ground, she kneels on the ground, she takes the yellowed old letter out of her bag and holds it with both hands, she stands up slowly and takes two steps towards Raghuveer)

Pari: "Grandpa, is this the letter? I found it behind your post box, in the dry leaves." (in a very soft innocent voice, holding the letter out)

Scene 3
(Corner under the neem tree, Raghuveer's trembling hands stop, he fixes his glasses on his nose with a finger, then he takes the letter from Pari's hand)

Raghuveer: "Yes... this is his writing... my Munna's..." (crying, the words broken by sobs, holding the letter to his chest)

(Pari sits down beside Raghuveer on the broken bench and puts her small hand on his trembling hand, the camera slowly pulls back to a wide shot of the neem tree, the bench and the old post office)

Raghuveer: "You really are a fairy." (smiling through tears)

END
